paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the King showed up, and He showed up GENTLE. Zechariah said He would come "gentle and riding on a donkey" (Matthew 21:5). No war horse. No army. Jesus is a King who comes close, and He doesn't need to scare anybody to prove it.

Now look at how He gets the donkey. Jesus tells the two disciples exactly what they'll find and what to say: "the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away" (Matthew 21:3). That's a King who knows the plan before anybody else does. I'd be sweating through my apron, but the disciples "did as Jesus had directed them" (Matthew 21:6). You can trust a King like that, even when His instructions sound a little strange.

Then the crowd shouts "Hosanna to the Son of David!" (Matthew 21:9), and the city asks, "Who is this?" (Matthew 21:10). Everybody has to answer that question, and it's the best one a baker can ask. The crowds call Him "the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee" (Matthew 21:11), and that's true, but there's more to Him. So keep reading, friend, because this story isn't over.
